senses.definition: A short list of things likely to go wrong, given in advance so nobody is surprised.
senses.caution: It is slide language and sounds odd in speech. If something is a real risk, call it a risk and give it an owner and a plan.
senses.example: Two watch outs before we start: the data refresh lands mid-demo, and Legal has not seen the retention wording yet.

cues.text: You are opening a steering committee update and want to flag two things likely to trip the group up, short of raising them as formal risks.
A colleague is taking over your demo next week and needs to know the two places it usually goes wrong.
Writing a one-page handover, you need a heading for the short list of things that catch people by surprise.
A friend is renting a flat in a neighbourhood you know well, and you want to name two things she should keep an eye on before she signs.

distractors: The one thing that must go right for the plan to work at all.
A list of everything already agreed, kept so that nobody reopens it.
Problems discovered only after a release has gone out to customers.
A written summary of what a meeting decided, circulated afterwards to everyone who missed it.
The set of conditions that must hold true for an estimate to be worth anything at all.
